body:
`parse.parse("{:tg}", "1/jul/2011")` raises `KeyError: 'jul'`.

`date_convert()` looks the captured month name up with `MONTHS_MAP[m]`, which is
case-sensitive, but the type patterns (`tg`, `ta`, `te`, `th`, `tc`, `ts`) are compiled
with `re.IGNORECASE` - that is the documented default (`case_sensitive=False`). Any
non-canonical spelling of a month name therefore crashes instead of parsing:

```console
$ python -c "import parse; print(parse.parse('{:tg}', '1/jul/2011'))"
...
KeyError: 'jul'
```

All six month-name types are affected (`{:ts}`, `{:te}`, `{:th}`, `{:tc}`, `{:ta}` as
well). Numeric months are untouched, and `case_sensitive=True` still returns `None`
because that only changes the regex flags.

## Change

```python
-            m = MONTHS_MAP[m]
+            # matching is case-insensitive (re.IGNORECASE), so normalise the
+            # captured month name before the case-sensitive lookup below
+            m = MONTHS_MAP[m.capitalize()]
```

This is the same normalisation the meridiem and `"Z"` already go through (bcf2f66, [LINK_REMOVED]);
this lookup was the one call site in that path still matching case-sensitively.
`MONTHS_MAP` and the generated patterns are unchanged.

## Testing

- new `tests/test_bugs.py::test_case_insensitive_month_names` covers all six month-name
  types plus the year-less `ts` form: fails on master with `KeyError: 'jul'`, passes with
  the fix
- full suite: `115 passed, 1 skipped` -> `116 passed, 1 skipped`
- 207 case variants over all 23 month spellings: no failures
- the type checks CI runs: `mypy --check-untyped-defs --disallow-any-generics parse`,
  `mypy --stubtest parse` and `mypy tests/check_typing.py` all pass

For transparency: this is the remaining call site of the month-name normalisation that
closed PR [LINK_REMOVED] bundled together with the meridiem/`"Z"` fixes which later merged
separately as [LINK_REMOVED].
